title: Retrieval improvements shrank when combined in a RAG pipeline
summary: Five changes to a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline each improved document ranking when tested alone. Adding their individual gains gave an expected score of 0.667, but the combined system scored 0.483 against a baseline of 0.412. The result concerns the tested retrieval components and queries.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5, Table 6, §D.14/Figure 9 and limitations on faithfulness additivity

evidence.tested: A matched component-composition experiment compared individual changes and the combined pipeline using NDCG@10, with a paired bootstrap over 93 queries.
evidence.unknown: The result does not establish that every retrieval pipeline shows the same interaction. The paper’s answer-faithfulness comparison used different component configurations and did not directly establish additivity.
evidence.ai_role: Learned query augmentation and cross-encoder reranking change query–document rankings; matched component perturbations test whether those changes add together.
